claims.title: How does the intersection acquire a basis over the power-series ring?
claims.hypotheses: The fixed rank-d étale comparison has a basis of surviving columns with integral periods after multiplication by τᴴ. The coefficient ring is W(k)[[u]], and the image of u has positive tilt valuation.
claims.statement: The intersection of the integral period module and the scaled étale lattice is free of rank d over the coefficient ring. Its basis remains invertible over the large Witt ring and changes the étale basis by an étale unit.

claims.title: How can two columns form a basis and still miss an integral vector?
claims.hypotheses: Use S=ℤ₃[[u]], its completed localization at u, and the columns of diag(uᵃ,1) for a≥0.
claims.statement: The integral quotient by these columns is S/(uᵃ). For a positive exponent the original basis admits a right inverse up to 3ʳ modulo 3ⁿ over S precisely when n≤r.

claims.title: Which later layer represents all columns in the new coordinates?
claims.hypotheses: Surviving vectors are representable by the chosen basis of the integral intersection. The projected layer maps are onto modulo the level and their period matrices have a common height H.
claims.statement: At each precision a single deeper layer supplies an integral projected comparison and a right factor over Ainf with product τ²ᴴ times the identity modulo that precision. The fixed scaled inverse of the target basis is integral.

claims.title: How can an integral period be written in power-series coordinates?
claims.hypotheses: The coefficient ring is W(k)[[u]]. The variable evaluates to the Teichmüller lift of a nonzero tilt element of positive valuation, and E is the Eisenstein polynomial of the datum.
claims.statement: A lifted basis of the period ring modulo (ℓ,u) gives unique coefficient expansions finite modulo every (ℓ,E)ᵐ. Its coordinate maps are linear over W(k)[[u]].

claims.title: Why do the coordinates of one period generate a power of ℓ?
claims.hypotheses: The primitive period satisfies φ(τ)=e(E)τ. At least one coefficient of E at an exponent not divisible by ℓ is nonzero.
claims.statement: For a fixed h the ideal generated by the coordinates of τʰ contains ℓʳ for some nonnegative integer r.

claims.title: Why does one power of ℓ suffice at every precision?
claims.hypotheses: One fixed period power has a coordinate ideal containing a power of ℓ. The coefficient matrix is over W(k)[[u]] and the initial right factor is integral over Ainf.
claims.statement: There is an exponent r independent of precision and both dimensions such that each right inverse up to τʰ modulo ℓⁿ descends to a right inverse up to ℓʳ at the same precision. For the tower h=2H.

claims.statement: The Frobenius matrix in the integral basis and its companion have entries in W(k)[[u]] and product E²ᴴ times the identity.

claims.title: How do the integral Galois corrections pass to the limit?
claims.hypotheses: The layers carry integral corrections on the full Galois group, the projected comparisons respect the action at the relevant precision, and their right inverses have a uniform loss.
claims.statement: The unique possible Galois correction at the target has integral entries and is invertible over Ainf. The resulting corrections obey the twisted cocycle law.

claims.title: Which two exponents can be chosen before selecting a layer?
claims.hypotheses: A fixed local field and Breuil–Kisin datum admit the infinite-order period multiplier. A frame to which the first assertion is applied already has a witness at the given order.
claims.statement: One scalar exponent normalizes witnesses of a prescribed order regardless of rank, height and layer. A second exponent provides invariant lifts to that order for every power series.

claims.title: How can one period witness work for the whole Galois group on the limit?
claims.hypotheses: The same target frame has integral comparisons with one loss exponent at all precisions. Every full layer is de Rham in the sense of the two integral witness tests, and the local residue field is finite.
claims.statement: For each order the target admits one integral matrix with the required scalar residue and a twisted defect divisible to that order for every Galois element.
